posts.cooked:
Welcome to another entry in my Footenotes series. Hope you brought your reading glasses.

Nightmist's deck holds so many bits and pieces of future content. We have picked a lot of them out, but everytime I revist her deck, something new jumps out at me. And then my head starts having thoughts (scarry I know).

Out of all of the villains and heros we have been introduced to through SotM, we know the least about Apostate. Seriously, we know a great deal about every other character except him. We dont know what he is, who he is, where he came from, why he has a sister sword to Fanatics, what his connection to Fanatic is as a whole...we know basically nothing. His bio is unhelpful, being all of a few sentenses and half of them deal with Fanatic going into hiding pre-redeemer status.

There a very important question here. Why. Why do we know so little about him? Why did Christopher choose to present him in this way while all the other villains get cool backstories and have all the fun.The only answer that makes sense to me is that all the answers to the questions above are somehow very important to the conclusion of the of the major narrative.

"It sends its servant" - Time Crazed Prisoner

Could Apostate be the servant of the Cosmic Entity and ultimate bad guy?

Consider the following. Nightmists deck contains a card call Astral Premonition. Flavor Text: "I shall not allow you to ravage this world as you have others". Others? He has brought chaos to other worlds as well?  Going back to the picture of Time Crazed Prisoner, there is a picture of orbit paths with big X's over the planet on each orbit. The name contains "Astral", so an astral premonition could be directly interpreted as getting a bad feeling from the stars (or outter space in general).

Oh yeah, lets also not forget that his front side is called Infernal Emissary. 

Emissary: Noun.

       1. a person who is sent on a mission to represent another person or organization

Man, Christopher kinda spoon fed us that under our noses! So is this person/organization that he is representing the Cosmic Entity? Take a look at his scant bio one more time. Group Affiliation: The Host. That sound familiar to you? Good, me neither. But the picture is starting to come together.

https://greaterthangames.com/comment/56932#comment-56932

Christopher putting "Demons" in quotes like that is more than likely significant to all of this in some way. Previously refered to them as nega-demons in the same thread. Putting both of those together, the conclusion is that these things are not Demons, at least not in the traditional sense of Heaven/Hell/Angel/Demon dynamic. They are something else all together.

The back art of Apostate's deck is incredibly strange and I am surprised it has not come up more on the forums. The thing in the center seems to be a planet on fire, at least thats how I'm seeing it now. The two females(?) bracketing that destruction though is quite a puzzle. Could one symbolise Fanatic, and if so, does she have a twin sister somewhere? That might even be too far a stretch for me. So lets stretch it further but in a different direction.

https://greaterthangames.com/forum/topic/footenotes-the-matriarch-and-the-red-herring-4239

This thread has a bunch of great stuff from a lot of different people. But one of the threads of thought that I really enjoyed thinking about was the loose connection we were making between Matriarch, the Cosmic Entity, and the Irish Morigan mythos.  The Morigan, just to quickly get to the point of this, is commonly depicted as a trio of sisters.

Well, this duo of sisters is rather interesting looking at it through that lense. Going back to my original thought there, maybe the one IS supposed to be Fanatic. Maybe the other is the Matriarch? Why Matriarch? Well, if any of my broad stroke conclusions from both of these threads is anywhere close to the truth, then Matriarch is very much tied in with the Cosmic Entity in a significant way. Now since it looks like Apostate is also the herald of the comming Appocalypse, both he and Matriarch could be connected in a significant way as well.

The Time Crazed Prisoner speaks of 'All will end as one' or something to that effect. "The Host". What if this Cosmic Entity is going from world to world trying to incorporate it into his own "realm" of existence? This could be the whole reason why the timelines and different universes are bleeding together, as a way to condense everything down before being absorbed/eaten/whatever it is it does. In a sense, he "hosts" all these worlds in his own realm to rule over and do as he pleases (or whatever motivation an all powerful cosmic dude might have). Re-reading KNYFE's bio, FILTERs interest in a particular set of realities is troubling. It seems to hint that there is one timeline that would allow this Cosmic Entity/Event/Whatever to consume the rest. FILTER doesn't mess with timelines "ending or begining", but KNYFE knows thats a lie. We are talking about possibly them aiding the Ending to all timelines, which would itself be the begining of a true singular universe. Why would this be good for FILTER? No idea, but considering the very nature of the Block and its inhabiting the gray areas of space/time, I would think they have the means to evade the fate of the rest of the multiverse. 

The bottom left corner of Time Crazed Prisoner shows one line that branches off to 2, which branches off to 4, which branches to 8, ect ect. This is pretty much how timelines get born in a sense, one action can yeild different outcomes depending on the factors of Fate and Chance (Nightmist brings these up as essential elements in her decks flavor text). Those all branch into unending possibilities and realities (ever see the end of Bio-Shock Infinite?). The Cosmic Entity, or whatever Cosmic Event that has KNYFE so worried, might have the reverse effect?

  1. 1a person sent on a special mission, usually as a diplomatic representatddf

In light of Silverleafs comment, I had to do more digging.

Remember our past discussion on Unity, Golems, and Jewdaism? Here is some notes also from Jewish texts on "fallen angels" from wiki:

"Jewish pseudepigrapha, especially apocalypses, he appears as the chief evil figure, “ruler of a demonic host, influencing event throughout the world, cast out of heaven as a fallen angel”

Also from wiki on "Heavenly Hosts":

“Most descriptions of angels in the Bible describe them in military terms, such as encampment (Gen.32:1-2), command structure (Ps.91:11-12; Matt.13:41;Rev.7:2), and combat (Jdg.5:20; Job 19:12;Rev.12:7). The heavenly host participate in the War in Heaven and, according to some interpretations, will battleSatan and Satan’s own army at the End of Days and be victorious.”

We can see the End of Days/Apocalypses relationship directly in Apostate’s and Fanatic’s decks. 

End of Days: “In Christianity, end time is depicted as a time oftribulation that precedes the second coming of Christ, who will face the emergence of theAntichrist and usher in the Kingdom of God.”

To me, it looks like Christopher flipped this old Christianity story on its head, where Apostate acts as the second coming of Christ trying to usher in the kingdom of the Cosmic Entity. The second comming is a direct result of the appearance of the Antichrist, and that seems to be Fanatic here.

Hey Christopher, how am I doing over here?

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Close, but a little off Foote.

I can speak to end times Christian theory.

The one you reference is a popular interpretation that was started by a scam artist/evangelist (it depends on who talks about them) in the 1800's.  It really took hold during the second big revival circuit in America and has stuck, and spread until it is the predominant protestant view of the end times.

(that was just for history's sake, not in game importance)

Apostate would very well fit the role of the Anti-Christ.  The Anti-Christ (in this theology) comes and unites the world, generally thought to solve a huge crisis or bring peace in troubled times, only to use that to usher in a world order that is evil.

The Anti-Christ is not the real bad guy though, just works for him, maybe an Emissary if you will.  He will lead the armies of evil, and of man against the True believers and armies of God in Armageddon, where blood will run as high as a horses bridle.  (that's pretty high)

The real badguy of Revelation is "The Beast," which used to be the UN, then the EU, you know, whatever group of nations comes about to promote peace and unity.  It has a bunch of heads and devours stuff.  (this version is simplified to the point of being innacurate, because no one wants to turn this into a week long study of popular Eschatology)

 

I honestly don't think >G is going too much into Revelation, that's dangerous ground to tread, as going biblical tends to get people riled up on all sides.  Are they using that imagery with Apostate and Fanatic?  Definitely.  The Host is the word for the angels, which all demons at one time were a part of.  It really fits his style and his deceiver side.

(Has anyone else watched the old Star Trek Animated Series?  They had an episode where they basically help Satan overthrow Heaven, only they stop at the last second.  It's hilarious.)

***

More history, non-game world stuff:

The old view pretty much takes Jewish Numerology and the format of the writing (Apocalypses were really popular then) and comes up with:

Hey Christians, don't trust Rome, Nero is Crazy, keep your stuff together, good times and bad times are coming, but in the end God will reward those who stay faithful and good.  He couldn't just write all that, because you don't get to write letters from exile without them being looked over by your captors first.

***

So let's run with this in game world:

Let's say Apostate is the Emissary of the big bad.

1.  The relationship between him and Fanatic has to be big.  Why would he make her, or if he didn't, who is she?  Is someone out there helping oppose the big bad, and maybe long ago word came to an Earth that wasn't ready for it and it became religion instead?

2.  Maybe Atlantis was destroyed by Apostate betraying them to the big bad, because they stood in his way.  We've talked before about how maybe all these artifacts are Atlantean in origin. . .

3.  If we run a little more, what about the four horsemen?  Conquest, War, Famine, Death.  They would have to show up if we go very biblical at all, they are major players.

Conquest:  Voss

War:  Maybe Cosmitron?

Famine:  ???

Death:  Gloomy?

Maybe we'll get a Voss alternate that is cosmic powered.  Or maybe these characters are still to come.

 

There is a small side of me that is now worried that Christopher has made this game just to run it into a Left Behind style thing, irrational fear?  Definitely; but nevertheless it is there now.  Thank you Foote.  I'm going to have nightmares about bad theology now.

 

Oh, as for Fanatic's fit into this, she would best fit as one of the Witnesses, who resist and preach the truth about the Anti-Christ, are killed by him, there bodies are left in the streets for three days while the world celebrates and then they get back up again, which would be somewhat shocking.

An "apostate" is a rebel against his faith/religion, a former believer who chose to "turn away", to use the christian expression, from his religion.

As Apostate has many things in common with Fanatic, it could suggest that "Apostate" was a former "Fanatic" - another "incarnation" of the winged hero of the faith, from the past (or future ?) who turned away from his "mission" and decided to serve the "other side" - or built his own army. I will stay far away from the supposed Cosmic Entity and other rumored big players - especially the force Fanatic worships, but the background of the Multiverse suggests at least two forces create/encourage with regularity "anormal" people on earth, who become heroes or villains and fight against each other, maybe in some kind of complicated chess game. Legacy and his strange hereditary powerset, the musicians of the void, the "born with power" Citizens, etc.

Currently, information is missing, and I spend more time wondering about the "concentric worlds" than anything else !

In the Mini-Nemesis thread, Empyreon was brought up and I think there is a bunch of relevant stuff bring to the table in support of my theory.

Empyreon is very close to the word Empyrean. From the wiki:

"The Empyrean was thus used as a name for the firmament, and in Christian literature, notably the Divine Comedy, for the dwelling-place of God, the blessed, celestial beings so divine they are made of pure light, and the source of light and creation"

Empyreon looks like he is made of Energy. Its bursting from him. He even damages himself in his AoE, representing the energy disapating from him into offensive output. 

More Christian symbolism is being used here, and if we are going to connect some dots here, that means he could very well be connected to the Cosmic Entity. He could possibly be a part of The Host in some capacity, especially if we are to stick with the Cosmic Entity as God/Creator metaphor.

Speaking of that metaphor, something else occured to me. When talking about all the Odin and Norse mythology symbolism in my Matriarch deck, I compared Odin to the Cosmic Entity there as well. Funny thing, and this is a little simplified, but Odin is a form of the word "Father". Sorta like God for Christianity. Thats not really important itself, but its more evidence for Matriarch could be a part of this as well.
